item.title: State Partnerships Lead – Eviction Data Response Network
item.description: About: Housing instability in the U.S. has reached historic levels. Across most metropolitan regions, housing costs have risen far faster than incomes, leaving millions of families cost-burdened and economically precarious. The country faces an estimated shortage of more than four million homes, while homelessness continues to rise, and more than 10 million Americans face eviction each year. The impacts of this crisis are deeply unequal. Black and Latino households—especially families with young children—face disproportionately high rates of eviction and housing instability, and the racial homeownership gap is the largest since the Fair Housing Act was passed in 1968. The U.S. does not lack ideas for solving this problem—it lacks a coordinated capacity to identify the most promising solutions, refine them through implementation and public debate, and drive their adoption at scale. New America’s Future of Land and Housing program is building that capacity. We operate at the intersection of research, policy, and implementation—clarifying ideas through research and convening power, supporting local leaders to test and refine them on the ground, and translating field-based lessons into broader systems and policy change. Primary Function: This position primarily supports the Eviction Data Response Network (EDRN), a groundbreaking initiative to create the country’s first large-scale eviction data infrastructure and use that data to keep more families stably housed. EDRN supports 11 state-level partners with technical assistance, financial support, and peer-to-peer learning to: Build durable eviction data pipelines that provide reliable, comprehensive, and regularly updated data on evictions statewide; and Stand up multi-sector problem-solving teams that use that data to craft policy and practice interventions that measurably reduce evictions. This position will serve as the primary liaison between New America’s FLH team and six state-level teams – Colorado, Georgia, Indiana, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Maryland – as they work to accomplish these goals. The ideal candidate is passionate about implementation of large scale change efforts, particularly for housing stability, with experience in coaching partners and supporting learning networks. Familiarity with court eviction data, eviction processes and housing stability are preferred. The candidate should be a self-starter and a good multi-tasker, and capable of working in a fast paced environment on a small, agile team, acting as a primary liaison between the state stakeholders in the EDRN and our team. The candidate should thrive on celebrating wins, driving towards improvement, and actionable follow-ups, acting as a coach to bring out the best in our EDRN cohort. Responsibilities: This position will be primarily focused on supporting the Eviction Data Response Network (EDRN) cohort of state partners, including but not limited to: Serving as the primary liaison between New America’s FLH team and six EDRN state partners, responsible for adeptly guiding them through their aims and milestones Duties will include structuring and executing monthly 1-1 coaching meetings, convening quarterly cohort calls, planning virtual and annual in-person partner convenings; Driving strategy and progress towards EDRN goals with state partners by ensuring project scopes, timelines and work plans are always up to date for relevant projects and assignments; Developing knowledge and policy products based on EDRN experiences, creating a feedback loop to enhance cohort experience while making connections between states and national technical assistance; Troubleshoot data-related barriers, including data governance, data sharing, analysis, and court filing collection; Interface with contracted technologists to support tech-enabled solutions for EDRN cohort partners and partner with colleagues on technology solutions for collecting and analyzing court eviction data; Monitor evaluation and learning, ensuring the initiative generates evidence of impact and insights that can scale nationwide; Convene and facilitate in-person workshops with associated logistics and agenda planning. In addition to supporting EDRN, which is the core function of this role, the balance of time will be focused on supporting the broader FLH team, including but not limited to contributing to the design and implementation of FLH’s domestic housing work, communicating with internal and external teams as well as additional responsibilities and duties as needed. Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree or higher; Minimum 5-7 years relevant experience, preferably in a U.S. housing, urban planning, public policy, public health, judicial operations, legal aid or a related field; Subject matter expertise in eviction prevention and/or civil court data (preference for experience with both); Strong and proven project management skills. In particular, the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, strong organizational skills, time management, and attention to detail, including familiarity with project management software and frameworks; Excellent facilitation, presentation, and communication skills; Entrepreneurial spirit and enthusiasm for finding creative and unique approaches and opportunities; Demonstrated interest in or dedication to fostering equitable outcomes across society, and especially for lower-income communities, communities of color, and other historically marginalized constituencies; Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of collaborative teams including both internal and external partners; Curiosity, eagerness, and ability to develop new knowledge and skills; and Ability to travel up to 20%. Compensation and Benefits: This position is a full-time role with benefits. The annual salary will be between $70,326.00 – $90,658.00 , depending on experience. New America offers a highly competitive benefits package that includes health care, dental, and vision coverage; a generous retirement plan; paid time off; observes all federal holidays; and an office-wide closure between Christmas and New Year’s Day. Location: New America’s offices are in Washington, D.C., with a hybrid work schedule. While a DC/MD/VA location is preferred, we welcome applications from highly qualified candidates nationwide. item.description: About: New America’s mission is to generate big ideas and bold solutions for a new America. We envision an America that represents and serves the public, where institutions work for all Americans, where workers, families, and communities can thrive, and where people are secure from existential threats. Primary Function: New America is seeking a visionary, creative, and highly organized digital leader to serve as Digital Director within its Central Communications team. The Digital Director will shape and lead New America’s digital communications strategy, including its website and digital publishing platforms, visual brand, data visualization, analytics, and responsible adoption of emerging technologies. The Digital Director will oversee four direct reports on the Central Communications digital team: The Front-End Developer, Digital Marketing Manager, Senior Data Visualization Developer, and Senior Visual Designer and Brand Lead. The Digital Director will establish priorities, support professional development, and foster an effective, collaborative team responsible for digital product development, marketing, visual storytelling, brand implementation, and performance measurement. Building on the successful launch of New America’s redesigned website and refreshed brand in 2026, the Digital Director will lead the critical next phase of the organization’s digital evolution: turning these foundational investments into sustained audience growth, deeper engagement, and greater influence for New America’s ideas. The opportunity is to move from launch to measurable impact—continually improving how audiences discover, understand, and act on New America’s work; developing more ambitious digital products and storytelling formats; strengthening the organization’s brand and reputation across channels; and building the systems, insights, and practices needed to reach new and evolving audiences. The Digital Director will define what comes next and establish a clear roadmap for delivering it. Reporting to the Vice President of Content and Communications, and working closely with other Central Communications colleagues, New America’s experts, emerging leaders, program teams, and operations colleagues, the Digital Director will translate organizational goals into a cohesive digital strategy and product roadmap. The ideal candidate combines strategic vision with technical fluency, sound management, creative problem-solving, and the ability to lead complex work involving multiple stakeholders and competing needs. Responsibilities: Digital strategy and product leadership Set the vision and strategy for New America’s website, digital publishing tools, audience-development channels, and data visualizations/interactive storytelling capabilities. Develop and oversee a digital product roadmap that aligns organizational goals, audience needs, and available resources, while ensuring digital products adhere to best practices for accessibility, user experience, privacy, performance, and search visibility. Lead product-development processes involving internal stakeholders and external vendors. Identify opportunities to expand New America’s interactive storytelling and data-visualization capabilities in ways that increase the reach and impact of its research and policy ideas. Evaluate New America’s digital systems on an ongoing basis and make informed budget, staffing, technology, and vendor recommendations to the VP of Content and Communications. Website management and digital publishing Lead the next phase of New America’s website strategy, ensuring that the site continues to evolve as an effective digital publishing, storytelling, and audience-engagement platform. Develop and manage a website roadmap centered on audience growth, content discovery, usability, accessibility, and performance. Partner with editorial, research, policy, development, events, and communications colleagues to understand their evolving needs and translate them into scalable digital solutions. Manage relationships with web-development agencies and technical vendors, including project scope, budgets, timelines, deliverables, and performance. Champion user-centered product development, incorporating audience research, usability testing, analytics, and staff feedback loops to inform continuous improvement. Establish clear governance for website content workflows, feature requests, quality assurance, maintenance, and publishing responsibilities. Audience development and analytics Guide New America’s digital analytics and measurement strategy, ensuring performance data connects clearly to communications and impact goals. Translate analytics into actionable recommendations for content strategy, audience development, and resource allocation across teams. Establish ethical, privacy-conscious standards for how the organization collects, targets, and experiments with audience data. Champion organization-wide fluency with digital insights, presenting findings in ways that resonate with both technical and non-technical colleagues. Brand stewardship Serve as New America’s primary organizational brand steward. Lead the continued evolution of New America’s visual identity to ensure that it remains distinctive, credible, accessible, and aligned with the organization’s mission and reputation. Partner closely with the Senior Visual Designer and Brand Lead and other Central Communications colleagues to maintain a consistent and high-quality look, feel, and voice across New America’s website, publications, events, campaigns, social channels, and other public-facing products. Establish and maintain brand standards, templates, tools, training, and review processes that enable colleagues across the organization to apply the brand effectively. Advise senior leaders and program teams on high-visibility brand decisions and identify opportunities to strengthen New America’s reputation over time. Monitor how New America’s brand is expressed and perceived across channels, using audience feedback, research, and performance data to recommend thoughtful improvements. Team leadership and organizational collaboration Lead, manage, and mentor a multidisciplinary team spanning web development, digital marketing, data visualization, visual design, and brand. Establish clear responsibilities, goals, workflows, and performance expectations while supporting staff growth and professional development. Foster an inclusive, creative, accountable, and collaborative team culture. Develop internal processes, guidelines, and service models that support effective collaboration on digital communications. Present digital strategies, product concepts, recommendations, and tradeoffs clearly and persuasively to senior stakeholders with varying levels of technical and design knowledge. Build productive relationships with external agencies, consultants, technology providers, and other partners. Emerging technologies and responsible AI Develop a forward-looking vision for how emerging technologies—including AI—can responsibly strengthen New America’s research communications, digital publishing, audience engagement, internal capabilities, and reputation as a public policy think tank. Evaluate and pilot tools that could improve content discovery, accessibility, workflow efficiency, audience understanding, data visualization, or digital storytelling. Serve as a vital member of the AI governance committee to develop responsible practices for selecting and using AI-enabled tools and ensure experimentation reflects New America’s standards for accuracy, transparency, editorial and research integrity, accessibility, and human oversight. Monitor digital trends and best practices and recommend investments that advance New America’s mission without compromising trust or quality. Digital governance, security, and operational resilience Partner with New America’s IT and operations teams to assess cybersecurity, privacy, data-governance, and technology needs related to the organization’s public-facing digital platforms. Maintain appropriate governance and documentation for critical digital systems, domains, integrations, administrative access, vendors, and account ownership. Support incident-response planning for website outages, account compromises, publishing errors, misinformation, and other digital or reputational risks. Demonstrated experience developing and implementing an organization-wide digital strategy. Significant experience leading digital product development, website management, web design, or a related function. Experience managing and mentoring multidisciplinary staff and building effective, collaborative teams. Demonstrated ability to develop product roadmaps, prioritize competing needs, and lead complex projects from planning through implementation and evaluation. Working knowledge of HTML and CSS. Familiarity with modern web-development technologies and frameworks, including JavaScript and React, and content management systems such as WordPress or Drupal. Experience with Google Analytics or comparable analytics platforms and the ability to translate performance data into strategic recommendations. Experience with project-management tools such as Asana, Trello, Jira, Monday.com, or similar platforms. Knowledge of current user experience, user interface, web accessibility, privacy, and digital publishing practices. Experience incorporating user or audience research throughout the product design and development lifecycle. Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated success collaborating with senior leaders and colleagues across diverse disciplines, roles, and levels of technical expertise.
